utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I take your answer as meaning yes, that you were the deputy Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. commander of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But there was no order to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, did you de facto perform the duty of deputy commander of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Can you explain to Their Honours why in the statement you gave in the police station and also in the statement you gave to the investigators you said you were an ordinary military policeman?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Because I didn't feel that way. Nobody listened to me or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you wanted to conceal the position you held in the military police of the Bratunac Brigade in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. Why would I conceal that when everybody knew it? (redacted) and Momir Nikolic know that I was never given a letter of appointment. I was just told orally that I would stand in for (redacted) when he was not around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, why didn't you say then that you were the deputy commander of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade in July 1995 in formal terms but you didn't feel duty-bound to perform this task? As far as I can understand you, you're saying that you had no letter of appointment, so you didn't feel that you were the deputy. But why didn't you say that, in fact, you were performing this duty but nobody asked you about anything? You kept insisting that you were an ordinary military policeman.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: That's what I felt like. That's what I said. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, I will read part of the interview of (redacted). It's in the B/C/S R0078311, where (redacted) says the following: "My name is (redacted) and by rank I am a sergeant but it says here that I am a sergeant first class. I don't know how come. This is a rank I had in the civil police while I was working in the military police. The next person was my deputy, and that was Mile Petrovic." If (redacted) says you were his deputy and you're saying you weren't, does that mean he was lying or, rather, not telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: He was telling the truth. I told you. I got this order orally. And I don't know -- how do I know who understood this in this way or that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, in response to His Honour's question you said that in this APC - and you don't remember the date - you set out on the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was driving?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were at the place where the anti-aircraft gun was.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was Momir Nikolic on that APC?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the command place, on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the left-hand side, where the commander stands. I apart from this APC, were there any other vehicles in front of you or behind you as you were driving along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road, in the direction of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there two APCs?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: It's possible. Who knows? Maybe. I don't remember. I don't remember whether it was on the first day or the second day that there were two APCs. It escapes me now. In that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road well, the road that you drove along, or not?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I remember the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what was happening as you were driving along that road?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean, factually?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean the sequence of events. Was there one APC or two? Were there any passenger vehicles? What did you see along the road?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: It was a long time ago. I know that on one day there were two APCs, but I don't know whether it was on the first day or the second day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to His Honour's question, you said that there was no megaphone in the APC.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: How would I know? All I know is that I didn't speak into a megaphone. That's the thing you talk into. It's round. I don't know whether it existed there or not, but I didn't find one in the APC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, I will try to quote you. When asked by His Honour about a loudspeaker, you said, "There wasn't one and I didn't use one."

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see one there. How would I know whether there was anything there or not and what things were there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what a loudspeaker looks like? Do you know what it is?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's round, and you hold it in your hand, and you talk into it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there one in the APC or not?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't see one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had there been one, would you have been able to see it?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had there been a loudspeaker in the APC, would you have been able to see it?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't go around looking for anything in the APC. Even had it been there, I don't know. I just climbed up and I stood there all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, in what capacity did you give a statement in the Bratunac police station?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: In what capacity?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Were you a suspect? Were you a witness?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I was summoned to talk about these events. I was summoned to the station. As I was summoned, I went to the station and I answered their questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give a statement to an authorised official from the Bratunac police station as a suspect or as a witness?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I suppose it was as a witness. How am I to know how they viewed me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you in what capacity you were being interviewed at the station?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: They said that they were gathering information about the events and asked me what I had to state, and I stated what has been recorded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that they drew your attention to the fact that you had the right to an attorney?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: To an attorney?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember? I can read part of the statement where it says, "He was informed that he had the right to an attorney, pursuant to Article 7 of the law on criminal procedure, that's an abbreviation for -- ZKP is the abbreviation for the criminal procedure of Republika Srpska. He was -- he said that he didn't need the professional assistance of an attorney." Do you remember being informed about this?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps. I haven't attended university, so it's not possible for me to understand everything that they asked me about. There are certain things that I do understand. And certain things that I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, did you tell the authorised official of the police station the truth in your statement of the 25th of August, 2003?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I told him everything I could remember and what I said was the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to a question from the Trial Chamber, you said that in that statement you had claimed that Momir Nikolic had hit one of the prisoners in the head.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you still claiming that this is what you said in the police station?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the police station, no, that's not something that I stated there. Not in the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can you remember that you didn't state this in the police station?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't state this. How do I know how it is that I know that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then who did you give the statement to?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: To Mr. Dugonjic, to the investigators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that you gave this statement to Mr. Dugonjic on the 22nd of September, 2003, after having given the statement in the police station?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: All I know is that I first gave the statement in the police station and then gave the other statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First you gave the statement to the police station and then to Mr. Dugonjic. If you told the truth in the police station, why didn't you tell the authorised official of the Bratunac police station at that time that Momir Nikolic had hit one of the prisoners with a rifle in the head?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: If I had known that it would be so important --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So why did this suddenly become so important in the statement given to Mr. Dugonjic?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: If I had known that, then I would have said that there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, were you told that it was your duty to tell the truth in the police station?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They drew your attention to the necessity of telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told that you shouldn't omit anything?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. How would I know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told that giving false testimony was a criminal offence?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So why didn't you mention this fact to the authorised official in the Bratunac police station, since you had been told that you had to tell the truth, that you shouldn't omit anything, and you were told that giving false testimony was a criminal offence? Why in this case didn't you mention this in the police station, yet you did mention this to Mr. Dugonjic?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, how am I to know? If I'd known, if I had known that I would be appearing here -- this is the first time I've appeared before a Trial Chamber. I don't even know how to sit here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I draw the conclusion that you didn't tell the official in the Bratunac police station the full truth? You failed to mention certain facts?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: If I had known that it was going to be so important, I would have mentioned this fact. How can I explain this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, please listen carefully to my question. Is it true that you failed to mention certain things to the authorised official in the Bratunac police station when you were giving your statement? You didn't tell the full truth. Please answer my question by saying "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. But had I known, I would have mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, in the statement that you gave to the official in the Bratunac police station, you said, "On the following day, I and (redacted) received an order from Momir Nikolic to escort several buses and trucks which contained Muslims. We were to escort them to Zvornik. I assumed that they were being driven there in order to surrender them, to hand them over, in the territory, in the direction of Tuzla. I remember that at the head of that long column there was a Golf vehicle, and Momir Nikolic was in that Golf vehicle." Is this what you stated?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct to say, when I interpret your words, that on the 14th of July, 1995 Mr. Momir Nikolic was escorting a convoy of Muslim prisoners in the direction of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think it's true or is it true? According to what it states here, it was true.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, he was there when they had organised that convoy, when the -- when there was movement, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, please try to concentrate and try to answer the questions precisely. I told you what you said, "I remember that at the head of that long column there was a Golf vehicle and Momir Nikolic was in that vehicle." You told me that that was correct.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I asked you whether it was true, that on the 14th of July Momir Nikolic was also in the convoy of Muslim prisoners being taken to Zvornik, he was escorting them with you and (redacted); is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. But I think that he stayed on in Konjevic Polje. He wasn't there during the entire trip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you say that he stayed in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: He was in that Golf and with another man who had a moustache.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, we're talking about the 14th, not the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: He was in that Golf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Momir Nikolic escorting the prisoners to Zvornik, to the school?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Not up to the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far, then?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: As far as Konjevic Polje. I think that's where he stayed. But (redacted) and I escorted them as far as the school, and someone else too but I can't remember who it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Up until which location did Momir Nikolic escort the convoy of Muslim refugees on the 14th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I think it was as far as Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You think it was as far as Konjevic Polje or you know this for a fact?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Up to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To Konjevic Polje. Do you know (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he a friend of yours?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: A friend?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Is (redacted) a friend of yours?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think that (redacted) told the truth?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why should he lie? He'd say everything he knew, everything he could remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, I'll now read part of (redacted) statement, which concerns escorting the Muslim refugees on the 14th of July. In that statement, he says: "You said that Popovic Mladic had issued the order to you. (redacted): "Yes." The Prosecution: "You also said you had informed your officer, Nikolic." (redacted): "Yes." The Prosecution: "When did you inform your officer Nikolic?" (redacted): "When we arrived or when I arrived, I think. I don't know. But when I arrived, I think that I saw him. I don't know. I don't know. He was there, but I can't remember." According to this exchange between the Prosecution and (redacted), it follows that Mr. Momir Nikolic was not present in the convoy of Muslim refugees. He remained in Bratunac, and (redacted) informed him about that escort after he had returned from Zvornik to Bratunac. So who is telling the truth? Are you telling the truth or is (redacted) telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I know that he was in that white Golf. He was accompanied by a man whose name I don't know but who had a moustache. We then continued to Zvornik, and they remained in -- they stayed on in Konjevic Polje. The Golf returned to Zvornik, where we handed over the people in the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, when you were asked by the Presiding Judge, you stated that Momir Nikolic spoke to two UN members in English. "I heard them speaking in English." That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, whether it was in English or some other language, I don't know, but it was a foreign language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, we can have a look at the transcript in response to a question put to you by the Presiding Judge, you replied that you had heard them speaking in English. Mr. Petrovic, are you claiming that Mr. Momir Nikolic speaks English?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, he wasn't speaking English, but those two foreigners, they weren't speaking in Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, in a question put to you by the Presiding Judge, you said that Momir Nikolic spoke to those two persons in English. Is what you told the Presiding Judge incorrect?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: That's not what I wanted to say. Perhaps Momir doesn't know English. I didn't hear him speaking in English. But one of the men knew a little Serbo-Croat, and they spoke together. One of the two UN members knew a little Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you now claiming that you did not tell the Presiding Judge that Momir Nikolic spoke to the two UN members in English?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps that's what I said, but that's not what I meant to say. I didn't mean to say that Momir was speaking in English. But those two UN members were speaking in English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, did you give a statement to investigators of the Prosecution from the OTP on the 25th of May, 2000?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: The 25th of May?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, on the 25th of May, 2000. I'd like to ask the usher to show you this document. The statement is in English. I don't have the version in the Serbian language, but you can have a look at the signature and tell us whether it is yours or not.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your name Mile?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your last name Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your father's name Milan?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you born on the 25th of February, 1967?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to investigators from the OTP on the 25th of May, 2000?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't remember? The translator -- the interpreter was Mihajlo Lukic. That's your signature on the statement; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's my signature. But I didn't speak to anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are now claiming that you didn't speak to anyone at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I did, but I don't know whether it was an investigator. I can't remember. But I don't believe I spoke to anyone. Well, where? Where did we speak? Where did we have a conversation?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. I don't know English either. I'm going to ask for assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Londrovic, my suggestion is that we have a short break. We have a ten-minute break, then we come back. During that break, you can consult with your counsel about that document. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at five past 6.00, a ten-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Londrovic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, just to be sure, is this your signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You very often say: "I think it is." Could you be more precise?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks to my learned colleagues from the Prosecution, I have managed to obtain the information. There must have been an interview with you in Srebrenica regarding the crimes committed by the Bosniak or Muslim side, crimes perpetrated by them against the Serbs. In your statement, 7 you say that your grandfather (redacted) was wounded, that your house was set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: That happened in Milici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Milici.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now I remember. It was in Milici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So have I managed to refresh your memory? You spoke to investigators from the Tribunal in Milici, and the signature is yours?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That took place in Milici in the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can remember this event?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, is it true to say -- did your brother die?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell this Trial Chamber when that happened. Who killed him? What happened exactly?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 14th of December, when Bjelovac was attacked, that's when my brother was killed and my uncle's brother too, as well as my grandfather.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 14th of December. You didn't say the year. Which year was it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your brother died --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your cousin died, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your cousin died, and your grandfather. Who killed them?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: How would I know who killed them? Muslims did. These were units who attacked Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these the units of the BH army who were attacking Bjelovac at the time? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as your brother, (redacted), and your grandfather and your cousin are concerned, why didn't you mention this fact, the fact that they were killed, when you spoke to investigators from the Tribunal in Milici?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean I didn't mention that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the interview that you had with investigators from the OTP, when you gave the statement, why didn't you tell investigators from the OTP that in the attack against Bjelovac your brother, (redacted), your cousin -- could you mention his name?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Subota [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your grandfather and cousin were killed.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: (redacted). Milos, but they called him (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you mention these facts to the investigators in May 2000 when you spoke to them?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, how do I know? Perhaps they didn't even ask me about it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But here you even say that your grandfather, (redacted), was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: That he was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here you said that you were also slightly wounded.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were bullet fragments that I had in the area of the kidney.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that in May 2000, when you were interviewed by investigators from the OTP, you were aware of the fact that your brother, cousin, and grandfather had been killed but you failed to mention these facts? In the year 2000, were you aware of these facts?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was, but why should I have spoken about this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you mention this to investigators from the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, how do I know? I wasn't concealing anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Londrovic, you've asked this question many times. I think we have to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, is it true to say, if you state before this Chamber that you are responsible for the liquidation or murder of two, three, five, six - the number is immaterial - Muslim prisoners, that if you said "yes," you would then be subject to prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, if, before Their Honours, you confessed and said, "It's true, I, Mile Petrovic, am responsible for the liquidation of two or three or a certain number" - it doesn't matter which number - "of Muslim prisoners," would by giving this affirmative reply, would you be exposing yourself to criminal prosecution? Please answer me with a "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I haven't killed anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not saying you have, Mr. Petrovic. But if you were to say this before this Chamber, if you were to say, "Yes, it's correct, I, Mile Petrovic, am responsible for the liquidation of two or three - the number is not important - of Muslim soldiers," would you be exposing yourself to criminal responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, how could I say that when I haven't done it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm saying to you again that I'm not claiming that.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, why talk about it then?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions. Thank you. If you will -- with your leave, my co-counsel would like to address you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, Mr. Kirsch, but you have to be very concise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Your Honours, thank you very much. I understand. But for the reason that Mr. Londrovic is not speaking English nor French and we hadn't had a chance to confer after this morning's hearing, I would like to ask some questions to this witness. I'll be very short on this with the Court's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Questioned by Mr. Kirsch:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, may I draw your attention again to the events of the 13th July. When -- could you please tell the Judges if you recall that Mr. Popovic was also in the area when you started the APC from the Bratunac Brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Which Popovic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know. If you know more than one Popovic, you may tell us.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: There was a Nikola Popovic with me in the police. Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this Nikola Popovic from the military police with you at that day?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: What day did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 13th of July I'm speaking about.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the name Vujadin Popovic tell you -- say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Vujadin Popovic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think he was a colonel within the Drina Corps at that time.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would he be the person in the white Golf, the man with the moustache? I can't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: Do you know anything superior officer from the Drina Corps with the name of Vujadin Popovic, who was maybe around the area of Bratunac at that time, July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I heard about a Popovic. I don't know if he's the one I was talking about or whether it's somebody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know Mr. Vujadin Popovic personally. If he would approach you today, would you be able to -- to tell this is the gentleman or not, to identify him?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I could identify the man who was in the white Golf, but I don't know who else you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you're talking about the gentleman in the white Golf, are you talking about the events on the 13th of July or about events on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: The 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember --

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: -- An escort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember having seen the gentleman on the 13th of July? I'm talking of Vujadin Popovic again.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I used to see that gentleman before, but I don't know what his name was. I mean the one who was in the white Golf on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Popovic maybe order you or your superior to go to the APC, start the engine, and drive to Konjevic Polje on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Do you remember when you were driving towards Konjevic Polje on the 13th of July that you were attacked by whatever Muslim fire then, on the street? Do you --

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall -- you don't recall any kind of incident like that?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: As we were going toward Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that this was in the direction of Konjevic Polje that this happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you drove to Konjevic Polje, was there any vehicle in front of behind you? The APC.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember whether that happened or not, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're not sure, or you were alone on that street within the APC?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't know. I don't remember. If I remembered, I would say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So given the statements you gave to the Bratunac police and to the investigators of Mr. Karnavas, it appears to me that it was only the APC on that road on that day. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: That's how I remember it. But as to whether there were other APCs around or not, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if you doubt if there were many -- maybe more than one vehicle on the road, you would have told the police or the investigator of Mr. Karnavas; isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: If I had remembered that, I would have said it. Why not? How do I know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the area of Konjevic Polje, do you remember a police car with a -- with a flashlight mounted on the top and a megaphone on the top on 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us a little bit more about that?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: While we were driving toward Konjevic Polje, the civilian police were calling on the Muslims to surrender.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you talking now about the 13th or the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: The first day, when we went there, the 13th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us exactly, please, where this police car you note, telling us about the first time, when it first appeared to you -- when you first saw it.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: While we were approaching Konjevic Polje, they were on the street, each with their vehicle, and they heard the loudspeaker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "when we were approaching Konjevic Polje," I mean, we're talking about the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, close to Konjevic Polje. All that belonged to Konjevic Polje. It was some kilometres away, near the crossroads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you first became aware of this police vehicle, was it in the area of Lolici, Sandici? Have you any recollection where that was?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I think it was closer to Konjevic Polje. There was that route there, but how can I remember that now? They were there in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you overtake this police vehicle within the -- with the APC?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: They were standing still and we passed by them and went on towards the crossroads and to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's your testimony today that this police car was not moving on the road, it was standing there, let's say 2 kilometres maybe before Konjevic Polje? When I speak about Konjevic Polje, I now mean the crossroads, where the one street is going to Zvornik and the other one is going to Milici.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Before that crossroads was the first time I saw that police vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was very close to the crossroads in Konjevic Polje actually?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, very close to it. Yes, very close to the crossroads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in Konjevic Polje with the APC, did you make another travel with the APC around the area on that day, the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the direction of Bratunac you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whatever direction.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as I recollect, you told us that you -- you went with the APC, you went -- when you arrived in Konjevic Polje, you took those two foreign gentlemen into the APC, went, like, 2 or 3 kilometres in the back -- in the direction of Bratunac, then returned to Konjevic Polje, and then eventually got back with Mr. -- with your superior and Mr. Nikolic back to Bratunac. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what I'm asking for, were there any further travels with the APC in addition to that one with the foreign soldiers you told us about? Either in the direction of Milici, either in the direction of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: On that day?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm only referring to the 13th of July now.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman by the name of Nenad Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Nenad?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nenad Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Deronjic -- Nenad Deronjic, that's a civilian policeman. Yes, I do remember him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know him? A person -- you could identify him?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see or meet Mr. Deronjic on the 13th of July in the area of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KIRSCH
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Questioned by Mr. McCloskey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These UN soldiers on the -- on the APC, were they riding on top of the APC out in the open or were they inside the APC when they joined you?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: They were on top, on top of the APC. They got onto the APC, and you could see them from the waist up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give them rifles and -- and tell them to shoot out at the surrounding side, the side to the roads? They were armed Muslims --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, witness, you have to answer this question with yes or no, because we didn't pick it up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were armed Muslims in the -- in the woods all around this road at this time, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those Dutch soldiers could have been very easily killed by one of them, couldn't they?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they could have been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you require those Dutch soldiers to stay out in the open on top of that APC in this war zone?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't require anything of them. They did what they wanted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After learning of what Mr. Nikolic said recently about allegations of you killing Muslim prisoners, did you talk about that with (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did I talk about it with (redacted)? In connection with what? With these indictments?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Listen to my question. It's very simple. After you heard about what Momir Nikolic said, did you talk about what he had said with (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk about it before you gave a statement to the Bratunac SUP with (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as soon as I read about that in the papers, we talked about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that before you went and gave a statement to the Bratunac SUP you'd actually talked about this incident with (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did. Before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, witness, I have a question: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How big is that armed personnel carrier?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: You mean how long is it and how wide is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Normally how many people could sit in that carriage?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Are you including the driver's seat and everything?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, everything.

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: About six or seven men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In that vehicle, are there some stuff in it, some equipment in it, or it's an empty vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: There were things in there, but I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, those things occupied a larger space, I suppose. Or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: MILE PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course they did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, thank you, witness, for your testimony. The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the next witness asked for protective measures. Because of the situation concerning of his testimony and out of caution, the Trial Chamber makes a ruling, proprio motu, to grant him the closed session. Yes, Mr. Londrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Your Honour, I suggest that the statement given by Mr. Mile Petrovic to the investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor in May 2000 be Defence Exhibit DS20. We tender it into evidence. We have only one version, in English, and it's on this disk, so we can either copy it and tender it into evidence tomorrow or you can admit it now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, generally speaking, any interviews or statements made by a live witness is not admitted into evidence, because we give the party the chance to cross-examine that witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that our proposal is rejected?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps while we're waiting, I -- I understand from the Court's statement yesterday and -- and from speaking with Court personnel that -- that I should offer the statements that were attached to our sentencing materials in -- well, if the witness is here, I can do that at another time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the closed session, please.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.04 p.m.
